static_traits.name: Zhang Wei
static_traits.family_status: Living alone, has a cat (named Speckles)
static_traits.social_status: Relationship with friends strained due to financial comparison; has a good friend but has not yet discussed financial troubles with them.
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems before; has not received psychotherapy.
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, fairly logical, capable of self-Reflection, highly cooperative; reports long-term Anxiety and Increased stress.

basic_info.main_problem: Persistently feeling I will never afford a house while doing Office work.
basic_info.core_demands: 'I want to see how I can change my view of this.' Hoping to ease the Anxiety and stress caused by the house-buying issue by changing perspective and reframing beliefs.
growth_experiences: After starting the current Office work three years ago, the feeling of 'I will never afford a house' emerged and gradually intensified from comparing with colleagues and others who own homes; strongly triggered whenever Seeing property advertisements or hearing others' home-buying news; tried budgeting and saving strategies, but the self-perceived financial inadequacy and inferiority have not yet eased, gradually affecting Work performance, Interpersonal relationships, sleep, and overall stress levels.

core_beliefs: I am a failure / inferior to others (my worth depends on whether I can afford a house)
I will never achieve financial stability (cannot afford a house)

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot afford a house now, it means I have no financial stability; I am just a failure.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Strictly makes budgets and savings plans, cuts spending to prove she is working hard.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never afford a house; I will always rent.

special_situations.event: Hearing others bought a new house
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not reach my peers' financial level, it proves I am inferior and worthless.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly comparing with colleagues and friends, focusing on gaps to drive myself.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am worse than my colleagues; I am a failure.

special_situations.event: At the company, sees colleagues making progress on financial goals (such as raises or buying a home)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Either reach the same financial level as others, or it is a total failure.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing on shortcomings and gaps, ignoring one's own existing efforts and positive aspects.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never catch up with them.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to gain financial stability and own housing, to be seen as 'successful' like peers and be recognized and accepted.
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being seen as a failure, not being recognized, or appearing inferior when compared.
defense_goal: Controlling Anxiety by maintaining high standards and constant comparison, avoiding exposing vulnerability
Avoids discussing finances with friends to reduce the chance of being judged

object_relations.self_representation: An inferior failure, financially unstable person

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether discussing financial Anxiety with close friends
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: If I talk about my financial troubles, the other person will look down on me and think I am a failure (Projecting one's own shame and sense of failure onto others' evaluations)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Avoiding elaboration, instead emphasizing 'I do not want to trouble others', responding in a brief, reserved tone, reducing emotional exposure.

manifestations: Uses 'I should be at the same financial level as my peers' as an inner rule constraining self-choice
Views 'owning a home' as a milestone that must be achieved; feels bound by the rule
outcomes: Sleep affected, overall physical and mental burden worsening

manifestations: Having close friends to confide in but choosing not to talk about financial worries
Withdrawal due to comparison in relationships, Relationship tension
outcomes: Increased sense of isolation, ongoing Anxiety

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Uses 'I should be at the same financial level as them' as the standard for self-evaluation
Using 'must / should / ought to' style self-Demands to measure worth

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Having good friends yet not talking about financial troubles, digesting stress and shame inwardly
Energy from self-blame and comparison turns to attack oneself, affecting sleep and emotions

positive_force: Can proactively try strategies such as budgeting and saving, has some self-management ability
Open to change, willing to restructure beliefs (changing rules into wishes)
Has a close friend to confide in (potential social support)
Clear help-seeking motivation, has preliminary willingness for action (further study, increasing income)
negative_force: Catastrophic and future-predicting cognitive biases (such as 'I will never afford a house')
Avoids discussing financial troubles with others, making support hard to obtain
Sleep impaired and long-term Increasing stress, further reducing functioning

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated self-comparison and negative automatic thoughts (such as 'I will never afford a house'), accompanied by Significant anxiety and stress
antecedent: Hearing news of others buying new homes
At work seeing colleagues' 'progress' toward financial goals
target_behavior.core_reason: Tightly binding self-worth to whether one can afford a house, with the inner rule of 'must reach the same financial level as peers', plus cognitive biases like catastrophizing and predicting the future.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding uncertainty and powerlessness, gaining temporary 'control' and an Interpretation framework through comparison and self-blame (but maintaining Anxiety).
target_behavior.consequence: Decline in work performance, Interpersonal tension, Sleep impaired, overall stress continuing to intensify.

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding discussing financial Anxiety and worries with close friends
antecedent: Thinking about confiding financial troubles to friends
target_behavior.core_reason: Fears being judged and seen as a failure, accompanied by shame and inferiority.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding possible negative evaluations and shame experiences, reducing exposure Anxiety short-term.
target_behavior.consequence: Social support not yet utilized, Increased sense of isolation, Anxiety and the problem maintained.
